subject: P04-11 held-profile, read-only classic column-layout reader
independence: Reviewer authored the separate P04-10 fixture plan/tests and persistence source audit, but did not author this two-file adapter. This review assesses adapter composition; it transfers no runtime credit from those artifacts.

findings.detail: Pre-requested stop returns Cancelled before any lease access. The existing loader validates held lease/name and identifies its existing directory descriptor. The new API only borrows the unmoved lease synchronously and never acquires/releases it or accepts a filename/path.

Fixed tables.config and ordinary core::Limits{} preserve actual loader semantics: valid primary wins without probing backup/saving; absent primary tries saving then backup; malformed present primary tries backup then saving. Read/unsafe/oversize failures propagate without skip. A parseable candidate must be a full dictionary; original manager recovery writes do not run.

Only loader Missing triggers bounded checks of the three literal candidates. Each read is checked for cancellation before/after; read errors are forwarded. Any observed present candidate converts ambiguous Missing to InvalidFormat. Missing success requires all three observed absent and returns both optionals absent. No enumeration or second recovery-selection algorithm occurs.

Pure projection receives the loaded unedited Document with fixed default limits. Empty loaded dictionary and malformed selected table/field facts remain engaged snapshots with accurate candidate RecoverySource; no missing/empty normalization. Owned core source/IDs move into result; local ConfigFile, lease, fd and raw borrowed views are not retained.

Pure Limit maps to Unsupported; Memory to Io; Root/EditedDocument to InvalidFormat. Loader/parser input-limit errors retain their actual loader InvalidFormat instead of being mislabeled pure Unsupported. Post-load, post-projection and prepublication stops discard results; bad_alloc catch gives observed stop priority and fixed non-config-bearing messages.

All data access is inherited descriptor-relative openat with read-only, close-on-exec, nofollow, nonblock flags; regular-file check, fixed maximum before buffer allocation, complete read and descriptor size/mtime recheck. Leaf symlinks and nonregular candidates do not become configuration. No new chmod, rename, unlink, lock, save, directory scan, payload/global-config read or file write is introduced.

practical_limits: Stop is observed at call/read/projection boundaries, not during blocking reads, parsing or projection; no prompt in-read interruption guarantee.

Recovery selection and Missing confirmation are separate observations, not an atomic filesystem snapshot. Replacement races can need explicit refresh and can return InvalidFormat instead of selecting newly appeared data.

Existing readFile protects held descriptor content by size/mtime observations; it does not promise immutable pathname identity or immunity to hostile same-size/mtime-restored external modifications. No stronger new claim is made.
Read access can update atime. Metadata/bytes preservation tests must exclude atime; acquiring the caller lease remains outside this function.
Allocation-error message construction can itself allocate; this boundary is not noexcept or an exhaustive out-of-memory guarantee.
Projection-only snapshot is not effective Java registered layout, UI application, sorting, legacy global resolution, migration, recovery rewrite or persistence.
required_parent_execution: Generated-profile adapter tests, deterministic post-read cancellation, candidate errors/precedence, byte+inode metadata preservation and snapshot lifetime remain parent-owned runtime gates.
